title: Pneumonia, lung abscess, empyema and respiratory arrest in the hospital
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the main lung condition (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/18/2026
Reason for Admission: Right-sided empyema

Hospital Course:
The patient is an 89-year-old woman who presented with acute shortness of breath and fever. Imaging and clinical evaluation confirmed a significant empyema in the right pleural space. She was admitted for stabilization and management of the infection. A chest tube was inserted to drain the empyema and provide adequate drainage of the pleural space. The patient received intravenous antibiotics throughout her stay. Her clinical status improved significantly as the drainage was maintained and the infection was controlled. She remained stable for the final 48 hours of her stay and was cleared for discharge.

Discharge Diagnoses:
Right-sided empyema

Discharge Medications:
Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875mg twice daily; Acetaminophen 650mg as needed for pain.

Follow-up:
The patient will follow up with her primary care physician in one week for a wound check and to review her progress.

Electronically signed, P. O'Brien, MD, 05/18/2026
refs: ICD-10-CM Tabular: J15-J18, J69, J85-J86, R09

distractors.why: Pus in the pleural space is empyema, not a plain effusion.
